entity_resolution.canonical_name: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Haytham
entity_resolution.arabic_name: أبو علي الحسن بن الحسن بن الهيثم

timeline_a_biological.event: Born in Basra, during the Buwayhid dynasty.
Summoned to Cairo by Fatimid Caliph al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah to regulate the flooding of the Nile.
Feigned madness to escape execution after realizing the Nile dam project was unfeasible; placed under house arrest.
Released from house arrest following Caliph al-Hakim's death; spent remaining years near the Al-Azhar Mosque writing and translating.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Began drafting Kitāb al-Manāẓir (Book of Optics) while under house arrest, establishing experimental optics.
Completed Kitāb al-Manāẓir, detailing the intromission theory of vision, laws of reflection, and early camera obscura observations.
Authored 'Al-Shukūk 'alā Baṭlamyūs' (Doubts Concerning Ptolemy), critiquing Ptolemaic planetary models on physical grounds.
Formulated Alhazen's Problem regarding reflection from spherical surfaces in 'On Burning Mirrors'.

physics_analysis.contribution_name: Intromission Theory of Vision and Camera Obscura Kinematics
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Resolving the dispute between emission theory (Euclid, Ptolemy) and intromission theory (Aristotle, Epicurus) regarding how human vision functions.
physics_analysis.hypothesis: Light rays travel rectilinearly in all directions from every point on an illuminated object and physically enter the eye to form an image.
physics_analysis.model_or_framework: Ray optics framework integrated with anatomical ocular geometry and dark-chamber (camera obscura) pinhole projections.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Constructed controlled dark chambers with small apertures to measure light projection from multiple candles onto opposite walls, proving non-interfering rectilinear propagation of light.

variables_definition.h_i: Image height projected on the internal screen

equations.validity_domain: Geometric optics approximation where aperture diameter is much smaller than object distance, but large compared to wavelength.
equations.assumptions: Light travels in straight lines in isotropic, homogeneous media.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Disproved emission theory; established mathematical basis for modern ocular physiology, optical instrumentation, and image projection.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Did not account for wave diffraction effects when the pinhole becomes extremely small.

physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Determining the exact point on a spherical mirror where a ray from a fixed point light source reflects to reach a stationary observer's eye.
physics_analysis.hypothesis: The point of reflection can be geometrically solved by intersecting a specific hyperbola with the circular cross-section of the mirror.
physics_analysis.model_or_framework: Geometric catoptrics utilizing conic sections (hyperbolas and circles).
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Constructed precise metallic spherical mirrors and graduated visual devices to verify reflection angles.

variables_definition.\\theta_i: Angle of incidence measured relative to the surface normal vector at the reflection point
variables_definition.\\theta_r: Angle of reflection measured relative to the surface normal vector at the reflection point

equations.validity_domain: Specular reflection on smooth curved conducting surfaces.
equations.assumptions: Mirror surface is perfectly spherical and local reflection obeys planar catoptrics relative to the tangent plane.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Led to a fourth-degree polynomial solution that challenged geometry for centuries, influencing Huygens, Barrow, and Newton.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Analytical solution required methods equivalent to modern algebraic geometry or calculus unavailable in the 11th century.

physics_analysis.contribution_name: Empirical Law of Optical Refraction Analysis
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Quantifying the angle of refraction when light passes across interfaces between media of different optical densities.
physics_analysis.hypothesis: The angle of refraction is systematically related to the angle of incidence, decreasing when moving into a denser medium, with refraction occurring within the plane of incidence.
physics_analysis.model_or_framework: Experimental catoptrics and dioptrics using graduated vessels and glass/water interfaces.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Designed a custom cylindrical metal vessel with angular graduations to systematically measure angles of incidence and refraction in air, glass, and water.

variables_definition.C: Constant index relative to media pair (early form of Snell's Law ratio)

equations.assumptions: Light travels slower in optically denser media.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Provided the most extensive set of empirical refractive data prior to Snell and Descartes; identified that perpendicular rays pass unrefracted.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Approximate geometric formulations were used rather than exact trigonometric sine ratios for small angles.
